teaser: Week 9: one agent drops the thread on mixed tickets, so you split TicketFlow into an orchestrator that delegates to focused specialists.

scene.title: One agent can't juggle billing, tech and product in a single ticket
scene.sceneHtml:
TicketFlow: Week 9

Complex tickets span billing, technical, and product issues. A single agent loses track of which sub-issue it resolved. You refactor to an orchestrator pattern: one main agent delegates billing → billing agent, technical → tech agent, escalations → human-in-loop agent. Each specialist has focused tools and prompts. Orchestrator merges results.

takeaways: An orchestrator decomposes the task and delegates to subagents with their own prompt, tools and model; only final results return to it.
Go multi-agent when sub-tasks are separable, context would overflow, or parallelism pays off; small tightly coupled tasks stay single-agent.
Multi-agent costs more (extra calls plus coordination) and adds failure modes like lost context in hand-offs, so it is not the default.
Hybrid: a deterministic workflow handles the standard 90% and an agent is invoked only at decision points such as an unexpected format.
